title: Rehearsing for the battle of bands at the Versailles
summary: The band practised eight hours a day in secret, with tan uniforms and Jesse Stone's arrangements, for the yearly battle of bands.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, as I said, I have named most of the fellows in the band --
Right.
-- and --
Of course we'd done that earlier on the interview --
Yeah.
-- but I wanted to get --
But we --
-- to that battle of bands.

I want to get to the root of how this all started. These guys were all thrown together and they said, "Well, we will show them. We will have a great band", and we would go practice eight hours a day just like anybody going to an eight-hour job, and getting ready for this big event that happened once a year, the battle of bands. There were 10 or 12 bands would participate in this --
Where?
At 15th and Versailles. It was the called then Versailles Dance Hall and this was the biggest dance hall in the black neighborhood.
Was this strictly a black audience for this battle of bands?

Predominantly, yes. It was, you know, not a -- it wasn't hardly a mixed crowd but there were a few whites and Chicanos and what have you that would come in but it was -- it wasn't enough to speak of. It was predominantly a black audience.
And this was a big event?
This was a big event. You couldn't hardly stir with a stick in this hall --
It was so packed?
-- it would be so packed and everybody was -- we were more or less the mystery thing. Nobody

knew what was going on. We kept everything a secret. We had beautiful band uniforms, black patent leather shoes, tan shirts, tan ties and white buttons on these tan suits and the band was really sharp.
Well nobody knew anything about this. We were getting ready. We were rehearsing. Jesse STone had somewhat of a book with a --
HIS own arrangements?

--his own arrangements and we had some stock arrangements and some of the -- along at that time we had big stock arrangements, you know, that were supposed to be just like the real arrangement, the charts and everything and he had quite a bit of those, you know.

Well, as we go on, we get ready for this big event this night and well, when the band -- we all walked in together. Well right then, we captured the audience because we looked so swell. We captured the audience right there. You know, it was our show from then on.
